overview: A browser asks for a resource, and a server answers with a status, headers and content. Follow a page request from the first name lookup to the HTML that arrives at your screen. Each packet can be paused, opened and read one byte at a time.
outro: DNS found the address and TCP opened an ordered connection. HTTP carried the request and HTML reply. The browser can now parse the page and fetch its other resources. Replay to trace each packet again.
steps: The browser splits the address into its host name and path. It first needs the server's IP address, then a TCP connection. The request will ask for the root page. HTTP can send its message once those lower layers are ready.

The client asks its resolver for the IPv4 address of www.example.com. A reply associates that name with 203.0.113.10 so the browser can address its connection. Cached records avoid another lookup. Each reply has a time to live that limits reuse.
A SYN proposes the client's first sequence number. The server returns SYN-ACK, and the client sends ACK. Both ends can now track an ordered stream of bytes.

The browser sends GET / to request the root document. The server answers with 200 OK and an HTML body. TCP splits that body across nine segments; the receiver puts their bytes back in order for the browser.
The browser parses the returned HTML into a document tree. It lays out the elements and paints the page. References to images or stylesheets would trigger more requests.
